players.product: Regulated electric service to data-center customers under electric service agreements (ESAs) with minimum take provisions

quarterly_data.signal: Duke Energy's 10-K (MD&A): working with state partners it won 87 economic development projects in 2025, representing over $30 billion in new capital investment and approximately 29,000 new jobs in its service territories, including manufacturing, logistics, energy and life sciences facilities as well as data centers - among them Amazon's planned $10 billion investment to launch a new high-tech cloud computing and AI innovation campus in Richmond County, North Carolina, on a site included in Duke Energy's Site Readiness Program in 2019. The 10-K calls supporting the increased generation load demands expected from such projects an immense opportunity for the company.
quarterly_data.figure: 87 economic development projects in 2025; over $30 billion of new capital investment; Amazon's planned $10 billion AI campus in Richmond County, North Carolina

quarterly_data.signal: Duke Energy's 10-K (Properties): as of December 31, 2025 the Electric Utilities and Infrastructure segment owned 55,713 MW of generation capacity - nuclear 9,404 MW, fossil 40,099 MW, hydro 3,762 MW and renewable 2,448 MW. Segment GWh sales were 264,008 in 2025 versus 258,668 in 2024; net proportional MW capacity in operation was 55,713 versus 55,139.
quarterly_data.figure: 55,713 MW owned capacity (nuclear 9,404 MW, fossil 40,099 MW); 264,008 GWh sales in 2025 vs 258,668

quarterly_data.signal: Duke Energy's 10-K (MD&A) on equipment supply: it continues to navigate supply chain challenges to acquire major generation and grid equipment components; it has executed longer supply agreements for solar panels and proactively secures equipment in advance of hurricane season; in response to accelerated load growth and capital investment plans, its supply chain organization has prioritized framework agreements with key suppliers to secure critical equipment and services, to reduce procurement risk and ensure cost and schedule certainty as labor markets tighten and tariffs and trade policies affect material costs.

Duke Energy's 10-K segment table: capital investments expenditures and acquisitions were $14,002 million in 2025 (2024: $12,263 million), of which the Electric Utilities and Infrastructure segment $12,553 million (2024: $10,689 million); the cash-flow statement shows capital expenditures of $14,024 million versus $12,280 million in 2024.
quarterly_data.figure: capital investments $14,002 million in 2025 (Electric Utilities and Infrastructure $12,553 million) vs $12,263 million in 2024

quarterly_data.signal: Duke Energy's 10-K: Duke Energy Progress applied (February 7, 2025) to build a second 1,360-MW hydrogen-capable, advanced-class combined-cycle (CC) unit at the Roxboro Plant in Person County; the NCUC granted the CPCN on October 16, 2025, and pending regulatory approvals construction is planned to start in 2026 with the unit targeted to be placed in service by the end of 2029. NCEMC notified its intent to co-own approximately 225 MW of the second CC under its existing supply agreement with Duke Energy Progress. The 2030 North Carolina retail revenue requirement for the unit is estimated at $113 million.
quarterly_data.figure: 1,360-MW CC unit; in service by the end of 2029; NCEMC approximately 225 MW
